A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we used a technique called Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy imaging (FTIR-I) to map the chemical and structural changes in the matrix of the osteochondral junction as a function of tissue region and age.
the cartilage‐bone interface is a highly dynamic tissue that undergoes age‐related changes that are dependent on both region‐specific tissue properties and the mechanical environment.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the osteochondral junction is not static and that it changes in a region‐dependent manner as a function of skeletal maturity.
the composition and structure of the cartilage-bone interface is not uniform, and it is not the same across the entire interface.
